transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-20
Time: 14:00 - 14:46 UTC (46 minutes)
Attendees: Alex R., Priya N., Sam O'N., Dr. Maya, Murali, Hannah, Ben

Summary: quick weekly pilot sync focused on onboarding progress, credentials and access gating, early benchmark interpretation, and next-phase tuning (KV cache / batching / quantization). Customer still deciding between hosted pilot vs reserved dedicated pool for final pilot scale; security cards (KMS, audit logs) are gating.

Topics: onboarding checklist status, VPN/VPC & KMS provisioning, initial latency/throughput numbers from Redwood shadow runs, cache-hit expectations, and scheduling an on-site remote run for end-to-end latency.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Rivera: hey everyone, thanks for the time. we'll do a quick run through — stan- — status, blockers, benchmarks, and then next steps. does that work?
[00:08] Ben Torres: yeah that works. quick note, i'm juggling two other meetings so if i drop off you'll tell me.
[00:12] Dr. Maya Patel: thanks, appreciate it. looking to get the latency picture solid this week.
[00:18] Priya Nair: great. last week we ran the shadow benchmark against your staging dataset — we pushed a 1k sample set with varied seq lengths. i'll summarize the numbers and caveats.
[00:27] Murali Iyer: quick housekeeping — murali here, infra. i provisioned the VPC peering request but there's still an IAM knob to flip on our side for the service account to pull logs.
[00:36] Alex Rivera: noted. Hannah, anything on the SOC2/KMS front?
[00:40] Hannah Cho: yes. we need confirmation of at-rest encryption with a customer-provided key. your doc mentioned KMS-integrations; is that customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) in the private deployment or is that supported in Dedicated?
[00:54] Priya Nair: good question. short answer: for Redwood Private we support BYOK via KMS/HSM integration; for Dedicated we can offer envelope encryption with customer key material in most cloud providers. there's some variance in audit log delivery depending on deployment. i'll follow up with the exact matrix.
[01:10] Dr. Maya Patel: and audit logs — we need 1 year retention and tamper-evidence for change events.
[01:16] Sam O'Neill: that's possible. we instrument event logs and can push to your SIEM via S3 or direct streaming. i'll circle back with the retention approach.
[01:23] Ben Torres: on the latency numbers, the email you sent shows tail at 420ms for gen-64 tokens. is that correct?
[01:29] Priya Nair: yes that's the 95th percentile on the shadow runs against our tuned model variant (quantized, 4-bit profile). caveats: the dataset had a large fraction of shorter completions which changes batching efficiency.
[01:40] Murali Iyer: what's your observed cold-start on KV cache miss? we can't have an initial user-facing 800ms spike.
[01:46] Priya Nair: cold-start for an empty KV cache was around 320ms on the same runs, but when we warm the cache with prefixes the p95 drops to about 190-210ms. these are with 8-way concurrency and continuous batching enabled.
[01:58] Dr. Maya Patel: that aligns with our expectations. where does the network hop factor in? our staging sits in eu-west-1 and some of your hosted nodes are in us-west-2 during the test.
[02:07] Alex Rivera: yes we observed an extra 60-80ms RTT in that path. for the pilot we recommended region pinning or Dedicated in eu-west-1 to avoid cross-region hops.
[02:16] Ben Torres: if we go Dedicated for the pilot, what's the commitment window and how quickly can you ramp GPUs? we want a two-week trial first.
[02:24] Alex Rivera: Dedicated typically has monthly reserved capacity but we can do a time-boxed pilot with a trial pool — it's flexible, but we need a little lead time to spin up GPUs in region. i'll follow up with options in writing.
[02:34] Hannah Cho: circling back to KMS, can we do an HSM-backed key in the private deployment? our compliance team insists.
[02:40] Priya Nair: yes private supports HSM-backed BYOK; for Dedicated it depends on the cloud provider's KMS capabilities and our onboarding contract. again, i'll send the matrix.
[02:47] Murali Iyer: on the network side, i still need a test subnet + service account. i raised a ticket last night but haven't had the ok to attach the role.
[02:55] Alex Rivera: understood — is there anything Redwood can do to speed that? a minimal set of IPs and a single service principal would let us complete the handshake.
[03:04] Murali Iyer: i'll try to get that approved by EOD today, but probable by Wednesday morning my time.
[03:10] Ben Torres: okay. on the benchmarks — can you explain the mismatch we saw between your shadow numbers and our internal bench? our internal runner had p95 ~300ms and your email shows 420ms — different tails.
[03:21] Priya Nair: sure. likely reasons: (1) your runner used a larger concurrency blend which improved token throughput but stressed KV eviction, (2) our shadow used model variant with a different quant profile, (3) network egress differences. we'll send a CSV with per-request timing to compare.
[03:34] Dr. Maya Patel: also, did you cap the batch size? we have a series of prompts that are long — single-turn 2k tokens sometimes.
[03:40] Priya Nair: in the run we capped sequence length at 1k for cost parity; when you hit 2k you see both memory and kernel path differences — that will increase latency. our runtime picks kernels depending on seq length which is why we suggested profiling your worst-case prompts.
[03:54] Sam O'Neill: can we do a small A/B: your internal runner vs our replay script, same dataset, same region? that should remove the noise.
[04:01] Murali Iyer: yes we can run that. i'll need the replay script and the CSV mapping.
[04:06] Alex Rivera: i'll attach both. note the replay script is minimal — doesn't do retries or backoff; it's intended to reproduce single-request timing and KV-warm sequences.
[04:14] Ben Torres: cool. another question — how does Redwood handle graceful fallback if Dedicated pool is saturated? we need guaranteed availability for the pilot.
[04:21] Priya Nair: we can set routing policies: overflow to a compatible hosted model variant and degrade to a cheaper quantized path if needed. you can also set an SLO for max queueing delay. fallback behavior and cost delta will be spelled out in the playbook we share.
[04:33] Hannah Cho: about logs — do you provide cryptographic tamper evidence or just standard append-only?
[04:38] Sam O'Neill: we can provide signed event digests and integrate with your long-term archive. i'll scope the exact approach.
[04:45] Dr. Maya Patel: excellent. anything on data residency? we need eu-only processing for PHI.
[04:51] Priya Nair: Private deployment or Dedicated pinned to eu region handles that. hosted might still have instances in other regions; we can pin routing for your account.
[04:58] Murali Iyer: i want to flag an infra constraint: our staging GPUs are cost-constrained so if we need to run large parallel replay we might hit budget limits. can Redwood throttle the replay to match a realistic concurrency profile?
[05:09] Priya Nair: yes the replay script has a concurrency flag. we usually recommend warm-up with steady concurrency and then a burst window. we'll provide recommended profiles.
[05:18] Ben Torres: ok. last block — golden answers. we asked for 20 canonical prompts; can you generate the evaluation harness to compare semantic similarity and false positives?
[05:27] Priya Nair: yes, we have an eval harness that runs BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and also embedding-similarity thresholds. but for generative outputs we prefer human review on edge cases. we'll share the harness and mapping.
[05:36] Dr. Maya Patel: schedule-wise, if we get KMS + VPC peering by Wednesday, can we expect a full end-to-end run with pinned region later next week?
[05:44] Alex Rivera: yes — tentative on-site remote run for Thurs or Fri next week; i'll send a doodle for availability.
[05:50] Murali Iyer: approved on my side contingent on the service account.
[05:53] Ben Torres: ok good. any budgetary flags? our procurement wants to see the trial cost estimate before greenlighting Dedicated spin up.
[05:59] Alex Rivera: i'll include a cost delta sheet: hosted vs dedicated vs private, with expected per-token and per-hour GPU burn for your workload.
[06:07] Hannah Cho: we also need the legal security pack — can you attach the SOC2 report and data processing addendum?
[06:13] Sam O'Neill: yes, will attach security.pdf and DPA template.
[06:17] Ben Torres: great. i just want clarity on success criteria: p95 under 300ms for 64-token completion, KV warm p95 under 220ms, and throughput of 200 requests/min per 4-GPU pool — we'll update and send that doc.
[06:29] Alex Rivera: sounds good. i'll add those as acceptance criteria in the follow-up email.
[06:33] Priya Nair: quick technical note — we'll include recommendations for quant profiles; for your 2k-long prompts we may suggest a mixed-precision kernel to avoid large latency spikes.
[06:42] Dr. Maya Patel: perfect. anything else?
[06:45] Ben Torres: no, that's it for me. thanks.
[06:47] Alex Rivera: cool, thanks everyone. recap: redwood shares benchmark CSV, replay script, security pack, cost delta; customer provisions VPC/KMS; schedule end-to-end run. we'll reconvene after the run to tune SLOs.
[06:59] Meeting end.

References and shared artifacts:
- Bench CSV and replay script (shared): https://redwood.app/sales/replay-NXH-2027-05-20.csv
- Security pack (SOC2, DPA): https://redwood.app/security/nexa-scan-2027.pdf
- Cost delta sheet (draft): https://redwood.app/pricing/nexa-delta-2027.xlsx

Note on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and stutters; timestamps approximate (every ~10-20s).
